# Validation: 0.1.0

## Unit tests (executed on Windows 11, Python 3.14)

```text
python -m unittest discover -s plugins/dv-netlist-equivalence/tests -v
Ran 19 tests ... OK
```

**19 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.** All netlists are synthetic, generated by
`tests/netgen_fixtures.py` in netgen's format (escaped identifiers with a
trailing space, bus bits, INIT literals, a `glbl` module):

- Self-compare of the base design: EQUIVALENT, no `random` checkpoints.
- Equivalent refactor (with `--strip u_core/`): every internal net renamed, an
  added instance prefix, LUT inputs permuted with the INIT adjusted, a LUT5
  re-partitioned into two LUT3, a duplicated register folded by register
  correspondence, FDR versus FD with the synchronous reset absorbed into the D
  logic (normalised next state), a carry chain with one XORCY replaced by a
  LUT: EQUIVALENT. Without `--strip`: NOT EQUIVALENT (unmatched used cells).
- Mutants, each NOT EQUIVALENT with the expected checkpoint and, for the INIT
  flip, the expected counterexample: one INIT bit flipped, two LUT inputs
  swapped, a register clock enable changed, a register removed.
- Wide-AND clock enable (24 inputs): the test first shows that the random
  signatures of the enabled register and of a hold-only register are equal,
  then that register correspondence does not merge them (the exact step splits
  the class) and that moving an output from one register to the other is
  detected.
- Input errors: an unknown primitive aborts with exit 2 and its name;
  `--dump-types` marks it UNKNOWN; a hierarchical netlist and a missing file
  give exit 2; `--help` documents the exit codes.
- `make_mutant.py`: flip and swap mutants of the base design are written,
  re-parsed and detected; the input-swap INIT helper is checked.
- Command line: the script run as a subprocess returns 0 and 1.

Python 3.8 syntax compatibility of the scripts and tests was checked with
`ast.parse(..., feature_version=(3, 8))`; only Python 3.14 was executed.

## Real-world use (anonymised)

The checker was validated on three Spartan-6 board builds of a hierarchy
refactor: 5.8k to 8.4k checkpoints per board, 0 mismatches, self-compare and
mutation tests passed. Mutation tests on those netlists (a flipped LUT INIT
bit, two swapped LUT inputs) were reported NOT EQUIVALENT at the mutated
flip-flops. After the generalisation for this plugin the released script was
re-run on one board pair and one mutant with identical counts, and
`make_mutant.py` produced flip and swap mutants of a real netlist that were
both reported NOT EQUIVALENT.

## Not validated here

- Other Xilinx families than Spartan-6 (their primitives abort the run until
  added to the cell table), Vivado netlists, hierarchical netgen output.
- Python versions other than 3.14 (only syntax-checked for 3.8).
- Live skill triggering in a Claude Code session. (`claude plugin validate .`
  and `claude plugin validate plugins/dv-netlist-equivalence` passed.)
